28 A beam of laser light is directed towards a narrow slit.
panel
cross-section
of beam of light
slit
After emerging from the other side of the slit, the diffracted light then falls on a screen.
What is the pattern of light seen on the screen?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the slit in the diagram is a short vertical line and the laser spot hits its centre.
Recall single-slit diffraction spreads light most in the direction at right angles to the long direction of the slit.
Compare a horizontal spread with a vertical spread and decide which is perpendicular to the vertical slit.
walkthrough: The diagram shows the slit as vertical and the laser beam cross-section centred on it, so light passes through a narrow vertical aperture.
A narrow slit causes single-slit diffraction, where different parts of the wavefront within the slit interfere and spread the light beyond the geometrical shadow.
The spreading is greatest perpendicular to the long axis of the slit, so a vertical slit produces horizontal spreading.
On the distant screen this gives a diffraction pattern with a bright wide central maximum extended horizontally, with fainter fringes on either side.
Option B shows the horizontal extended pattern perpendicular to the vertical slit. This is option B.

A.explanation: A small dot would mean no significant spreading, but a narrow slit causes strong single-slit diffraction and spreading of the beam.

B.explanation: The vertical slit diffracts light mainly in the horizontal direction, so the central maximum is a horizontal band perpendicular to the slit.

C.explanation: A vertical band is parallel to the slit, but single-slit spreading is greatest in the direction perpendicular to the slit length.

D.explanation: A large circular spot would mean equal spreading in all directions, but a slit spreads light mainly in one direction.
